methods.slims: 196 ELM classes, multi-criteria composite scoring (pre-defined weights, non-circular)
methods.structural: Sequence-based exposure estimation (AlphaFold unavailable for HSV-1)

key_conclusion: HSV-1 neurovirulence specificity arises from qualitative molecular mechanisms (ICP34.5-Beclin1 autophagy inhibition, US3-PKA apoptosis modulation, pUL37-TRAF6 innate immunity suppression) rather than quantitative differences in disorder content, SLiM density, or CNS pathway breadth. All three targets employ validated molecular mimicry strategies recovered by computational analysis.
limitations: No AlphaFold structures for HSV-1 proteins (exposure estimates sequence-based only)
Small sample size (3 targets vs 8 controls) limits statistical power; post-hoc power analysis confirms tests are severely underpowered
Conservation analysis limited to target proteins (ortholog sequences needed for controls)
GTEx brain TPM as proxy for CNS specificity (not cell-type resolved)
